title: Deep learning stratifies postoperative cholangiocarcinoma recurrence risk in a multicenter cohort
summary: A neural classifier used 12 clinical factors to stratify postoperative intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma into higher- and lower-recurrence-risk groups. Development pooled 1,421 patients from three centers, with evaluation in 234 patients from another center; the source reports AUC 0.78 for the framework versus 0.60 for AJCC staging and 0.70 for a Cox model. Retrospective subgroup analyses also associated adjuvant treatment with better outcomes in the higher-risk group. Treatment was not randomized, so these comparisons do not demonstrate a causal treatment-selection benefit or justify clinical deployment.
ai_technology: Fully connected neural network with Cox-screened clinical features
organization: Renji Hospital, Shanghai Jiao Tong University; Second Military Medical University; Fudan University; Fujian Medical University

evidence.tested: Retrospective derivation 1,421 patients/three centers and 234 patients/fourth center. Model recurrence-risk groups differed in survival; observational treatment subgroup comparisons remained nonrandomized.
evidence.unknown: External retrospective cohort is not independent-team replication or prospective use. Treatment associations can be confounded; outcomes after algorithm-guided treatment were not evaluated.
evidence.ai_role: A learned neural network mapped 12 Cox-screened clinical factors to recurrence-risk classes, enabling disease-specific prognostic stratification.

source_review.scope: Independent primary full Abstract, patient/network/prognostic-subtype Methods, relevant Results and Discussion; visible publication/accepted dates and affiliations. No supplement review.
